::: {.doc-subject}

Fit each step in order on the training data.
:::

::: {.doc-usage-source}
Usage

[Source](https://github.com/tidymodels/shoez/blob/examples-section/shoez/recipe.py#L330-L462){target="_blank" rel="noopener"}
:::

::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION}
```python
Recipe.fit(data)
```
:::

::: {.doc-text}

The transformed output of step *i* is the input to step *i+1*'s
``fit()``, so later steps see the schema as modified by earlier ones.
``RowOp`` steps *are* applied here — a row operation reshapes the
training frame every later step then fits on — but never run during
``transform()`` on new data, which the framework enforces structurally.

Each fit works on *copies* of the steps, so the recipe is left unchanged
and refittable, and a `FittedRecipe` never shares fitted state with the
recipe or with another fit of it.
:::

## Examples {.doc-examples}

``fit()`` estimates each step's statistics on the training data and
returns a `FittedRecipe` with the selectors resolved to concrete
columns:



::: {#f1dc6f35 .cell execution_count=2}
``` {.python .cell-code}
df = pd.DataFrame(
    {"age": [25, 41, 33, 52], "city": ["NYC", "LA", "NYC", "SF"]}
)
(
    Recipe()
    .add(StepNormalize(s.numeric_predictors()))
    .add(StepDummy(s.nominal_predictors()))
    .fit(df)
)
```

::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2}
```
Recipe (trained)
  Inputs: 3 columns — 3 predictors
  Steps:
    step_normalize(age)                   [trained]
    step_dummy(city → city_NYC, city_SF)  [trained]
```
:::
:::
